# Episode stories: does each one stand alone?

## Queen Sunduk (partly)

The last woman of the bone wants to know she can be king; a court that hates the word 'woman' and her own feeling for Yushin stand in the way; the turn is Yushin asking her to say his name once before titles take over; she is crowned, then reads Taizong's scentless peonies and wins the first round by reading people.

**Fixes:** Too many openings before the heroine: Munhee's hair, the hill, the palace ride and the bone lecture all come before Sunduk speaks at block 25. Keep 'A Queen? Ridiculous.', then cut the family material to one beat (Bupmin's 'no bone' line). Order is broken: the 'last day for it' name exchange (42–53) happens after she is crowned (30) and after the yard ogling. Move 34–53 (Yushin intro, yard, east-star flashback, name exchange) before block 30, so the crowning lands on 'Your Majesty. Nothing else.' Block 6 says 'two children' but block 3 already has Inmun, so there are three. Block 11 has Munhee on the hill, though she was last seen at her hair. Block 50 ('last time in forty-one years that anyone calls him that') is contradicted by Pumsuk, where Sunduk says 'Yushin.' again. The envoy montage (61–73) should end on the peonies, which are her best beat. Move Jomei's line before the peony gift, then the name hanja and the card.

## Harmony Council (yes)

Six nobles must agree on a king by dawn and three refuse a woman; the youngest, Bidam, stands up out of turn; Alchun's tiger line turns the last hand; six to nothing, and Bidam and Yushin go back to their 108-all rivalry.

**Fixes:** A tight single-room scene. It needs: (1) the council members (Murim, Imjong, Suljong, Yumjang) speak with no introduction. One narrator line seating the six would help. (2) The count is off: seven men speak (Bidam, Yushin and the five elders), but the text says six sleeves. Make Bidam the seventh, or drop one. (3) The Lotus Sutra dragon-girl quote (29) floats after the vote. Put it right after Bidam's speech, or cut it. (4) The tiger quote retells Alchun's line, which breaks the 'one telling per event' rule. Keep one.

## Jinheung, the Cloud (partly)

The Cloud King makes Silla big with stones and a yard of boys, then shaves his head; the old men still can't decide if 'cloud' is praise.

**Fixes:** This is an essay, not a story. Nobody wants anything on the page, and the herald/elder voices are anonymous. Give it one scene: Jinheung at a stone with the herald, or the day he shaves his head with the court still saying Majesty. The Hwarang paragraphs (8–12) can carry a line from that scene. Handoff in and out is good. The elder's 'Gwansan' tease sets up The Severing well; don't explain it further here.

## Prince Euija (yes)

Five days before he is made crown prince, Euija needs a champion who belongs to no clan; an eel boy with no name dives five days for a Jinmo burner; the prince saves him from the river, steals his father's crown to summon the deer, names him Buyeo Gyebek and puts him on the sand.

**Fixes:** Benchmark. Minor: the closing 'Five days' recap flashback (111) repeats lines the reader just heard and could be cut. The last card hands straight into the tourney, so Eight Great Clans must pick up on the sand without restarting the day (see that entry).

## Eight Great Clans (partly)

The eight houses fight over the king's sons and the river berths; on the crown prince's day their boys fight it out on chalk and sand, and Gyebek outlasts the Jinmo boy; nothing is settled, and Elder Satek turns his thumb down for reasons he never explains.

**Fixes:** Handoff problem. Prince Euija ends with the herald reading names and 'Eight boys on the sand'. This episode opens with Heewon's clan roll (keep it), then ten term cards, then block 12 restarts 'On the crown prince's day' as if it were a new day. Move the term cards (3–11) down into the Assembly section and go from the roll straight to the sand. Block 12 refers to 'the west bridge', which isn't mentioned until block 39; plant it first or cut the reference. Block 22 still calls Gyebek 'the crown prince's nobody' after Prince Euija named him on that same sand. Say 'Buyeo Gyebek', or 'the eel boy with the royal name'. Make his bout the climax and end the tourney there. The Rock term and diagram are repeated in King Euija and Yunchung. Keep one telling (Yunchung, where it matters) and trim the Assembly half here to the Satek/Yunbi feud. Better last beat: the unexplained thumb (47), but only if it pays off later. If it never fires, cut it.

## Gunchogo, the 13th (no)

Baekje's thirteenth king marches north and a Goguryeo king dies on his own wall; the chant 'restore the thirteenth' is born.

**Fixes:** No scene, two quotes for the same arrow (3 and 4), and a third quote about the Seven-Branched Sword. Keep one quote and dramatize one moment: the stray arrow on the Pyongyang wall seen from the Baekje side, or the crown prince handing over the sword. Block 9 spends King Euija's 'a country is a story' line and says it 'gets Daeya burned', which spoils the Daeya arc. Soften it to a tease. The handoff in (from Eight Great Clans) and out (to Commander Yeon) works.

## Commander Yeon (partly)

Yeon holds the frontier by terror and builds a wall; he takes in a Mohe boy who guards a burned house and names him Gulgul; his father hands him the seal and sends him to Pyongyang with one instruction, 'say half'.

**Fixes:** Biggest order bug in the range. The traitor is asked 'Do you know what happens to traitors' (4), executed (5), and then interrogated again with the same question (11–13) after he is dead. Move 11–13 to replace 4 and keep the execution after them. Block 14 says 'A month before the Summit', but the Summit isn't introduced until the summons at 36. Change it to 'a month before the summons', or move the summons earlier. The heart of the episode is Gulgul. The North Wall flash-forward (30–35) is lovely but needs its header. The summons should come back as the last scene so 'say half' sets up the next card. 'Manchuria' is a modern word; 'the high mountains of the north' is better.

## High Summit (partly)

Yeon wants the court ready for the Second Emperor; five commanders and his uncle want to split a granary; threatened with the word 'traitor', he walks out to a cheering yard; that night his first son is born.

**Fixes:** The council fight works and has real moves. The Namseng birth is tacked on: it needs the bridge, or should move to open Academy. Blocks 35 and 37 read like image prompts ('no extra bodies, no portrait-frame crowd', 'The portrait does not stay paint'). Rewrite them as storyteller narration. The opener lecture (3–7: quote, term, diagram, table) delays Yeon's entrance. Bring 'Pyongyang already knows the sound of those hooves' up against the chamber noise.

## Gwanggaeto, the Great King (no)

Silla begs Goguryeo for help, the Great King's horsemen clear the Wa, and then stay for fifty years.

**Fixes:** Essay. Blocks 2 and 3 repeat each other ('sixty-four fortresses… the stele'), and the Stele episode will say it again. Dramatize the Silla king's begging letter, or the horsemen riding into Surabol and not leaving. The strongest idea is the tease in block 9: a Silla prince will one day ask a foreign emperor for an army. The last card then pivots to Bupmin's Hwarang rules, which has nothing to do with it. Either point the card at Bupmin through 'what Silla never forgets', or move this episode next to Chunchu's Tang mission.

## Bupmin (partly)

At fifteen Bupmin trains under his uncle; Yushin asks which of the five rules he will break first; the boy who always pulls up behind his sister answers 'retreat', meaning he refuses to be only a follower.

**Fixes:** The ending works, but the middle is world-building: clubs, cypress, handicaps (9–12). Cut most of it, or give it to a character with a want. Plant Bupmin's want early: he is tired of following Gotaso and his father. The 'retreat' answer then pays it off. The 641 jump from Gwanggaeto is abrupt. The opener is fine, but the map/diagram could follow the first scene.

## Sadaham (yes)

Under the eaves Yushin tells the new boys about two first-class friends who swore 'one dies, the other follows'; Mugwan dies of a cough and Sadaham keeps the swear by not eating for seven days.

**Fixes:** A strong frame tale, and the flashbacks are well marked. Drop the Yamato Mimana quote (16) and keep only the gate quote, which Yushin then waves away. The boys' frame interjections are good. The card into Gotaso works.

## Gotaso (partly)

A girl who does what she wants falls for showy Pumsuk at a gyuku match and names their four children before he has asked her father; first, a prologue in which her father goes silent and does something unwritten at a ford to get her back.

**Fixes:** Two stories. The abduction is Chunchu's story: it plants his rage at losing his one daughter, and it is the better half. The romance has no obstacle, since everyone is on her side. Either give the romance resistance (Munhee doubts Pumsuk's flash; Pumsuk's rank), or open on the gyuku match and move the abduction to Pumsuk as Chunchu's reason for the vow. Ages: 'two springs earlier' still says (16), and the gyuku match says (16) again. The monologue at block 5 has no speaker. Is it Chunchu, from later? Mark it. Munhee speaking on the nineteen-li walk home (19) implies she rode out too; set that up.

## Pumsuk (partly)

Gotaso marries Pumsuk after Chunchu makes him swear on his life; while the newlyweds leave for the border, the Queen and Yushin stay in the empty hall and almost say it.

**Fixes:** The title is Pumsuk, but the spine is Sunduk and Yushin, and the opener (0) recaps Gotaso instead of hooking. Open on the vow ('If anything happens to her, you know I'm going to kill you'). Chronology bounces three times: Daeya departure (22) → back in the hall (24) → outside (55) → back to the feast (57). Move 22–23 to just before the closing card, and move Haesang (57–59) before the empty hall, or cut him. The girl-child flashback (10) reads like an image prompt. Sunduk's 'Your son's girl' is wrong (Chunchu is not her son), and 'that doorway has taken three' and Chunmyung's 'Four' are unreadable. Explain them or cut them.

## Munhee (partly)

Munhee buys her sister's dream for a skirt, mends Chunchu's torn coat, and keeps him; when she is pregnant and he still hasn't proposed, Yushin lights a pyre where the Queen can see it, and Chunchu shouts 'It's me!'; they marry, Bupmin is born, and Chunchu puts down his star.

**Fixes:** The best comic engine in the range (dream sale → torn coat → pyre) is buried by the 'Closed Months' section (46–63), which runs eighteen blocks and repeats the same beat. Trim it to two or three. The frame break at 28 needs the bridge. Before the pyre, plant Chunchu's delay and the pregnancy. Bupmin's birth says 'Years later', which is wrong; it is the next year. Block 68 ('Chunchu stopped going to the hill') contradicts Queen Sunduk, where six-year-old Bupmin finds him on the hill. Pick one.

## Academy (partly)

Yeon marches his eldest to school in his boots, says the sutra can be skipped because the monks own the farms, and makes an enemy of a sweeping monk and his own uncle.

**Fixes:** Namseng's want ('be told he did well') is set up and never paid off. End on him reading his father's unopened Daodejing, and add one line where he hopes Yeon notices. Bodeok is a Chekhov plant; make sure he fires later. Stele (10 blocks) and Dosuryu (18 blocks) are fragments of the same Yeon household. Consider merging Academy + Stele + Dosuryu into one episode: school, rock, boots, list.

## Stele (no)

Yeon shows his sons the Great King's sixty-four fortresses and asks how that country now bows to Chang'an.

**Fixes:** A single beat with three quotes. Fold it into Academy as its closing scene, or into Dosuryu as the opener ('the boots' line then lands in the same house). Cut one of the two Tang tribute quotes (7 and 8).

## Dosuryu (partly)

Dosuryu walks in with his boots on to warn Yeon that the king and his uncle mean to kill him by spring; Yeon laughs, stops, and decides to make a longer list.

**Fixes:** A sharp single scene, but too slight to stand alone. Merge it with Stele/Academy. Keep one of the two 'the plan leaked' quotes (11 and 12), not both. The last line is the right cliffhanger.

## King Euija (partly)

Crowned at last, Euija fakes a dragon and a run of cheap miracles to own the country's story; Gyebek refuses to call paper a dragon and Seongchung asks what happens when the people find out; at the feast he sends his quiet son Pung away as a hostage.

**Fixes:** Three detours dilute it: the court-maid chamber scene (48–59), the nation chant (60), and the Gyebek age note (61). Keep the maids to one beat. Block 47 ('it is the sentence that kills him… word for word') follows narration, so the reader can't tell which sentence. Name it ('Nobody inspects the evidence…'). The 'general' card at 9 conflicts with 61 ('passed over every season'). The name 'Rock of Politics' here vs 'Rock of Government' in Eight Great Clans should be unified. A better last beat already exists: Pung asking 'For how long?'

## Yunchung (partly)

Euija wants his country back off the Rock without a civil war; Yunchung says 'win a war abroad'; Euija sells the Assembly a crisis story and sends Yunchung with ten thousand men to Daeya.

**Fixes:** The title character vanishes after block 10 and returns for two lines at the end. Put Yunchung in the Assembly scene and let him be the one who says 'Daeya' (from the frontier he knows). The Rock quote and diagram (18–19) repeat King Euija and Eight Great Clans; keep only one. Gyebek's 'not you' exchange needs setup (bridge). Yunchung's 'Then we're done for, plain and simple' (44) reads as defeatism right before he promises Daeya by autumn. Clarify (does he mean 'then it's settled'?). Euija's long run of single-speaker lines (22–27, 35–42) breaks the 'someone should interrupt' rule; let Chunbok or Seongchung cut in once.

## The Severing (yes)

King Seong loses the river to his own ally, marches to take it back, rides out at night to steady his son, and is caught in a ditch where a slave takes his head on the Cloud King's order.

**Fixes:** Strong. Two cautions. (1) Muryuk's mystery box: the text doesn't name him, but the speaker id 'muryuk' on dialogue blocks 15 and 21 may render his name as the speaker label in the UI. Check that, and use an unnamed label until his episode. (2) Kingsung's 'A prince of Geumgwan' gives away nearly everything. Make it just 'Gaya…?'. The Hamsan quote (8) can go. The handoff in (Gyebek's 'What is the Severing') and out (Gumil card) works.

## Gumil (no)

Gumil, a yellow-sleeve clerk with a wife every man stares at and pay that buys her nothing, wants to count for something in a country that ranks bones; a True Bone boy is put over him at Daeya, and the episode ends with that boy unable to sleep after watching Maehwa at the feast.

**Fixes:** The title character first appears at block 96 of 136. Blocks 0–92 are Yushin at the steam cavern (including a 75-block First Kim flashback that the Seohyun episode will also tell), then BOTH ROADS and Chunchu's steam visit. The previous episode ended on 'Its grain clerk is called Gumil. Remember that name…!', so the reader lands in the wrong story. Move blocks 0–92 into their own cavern episode, and merge them with the other steam scenes scattered through Siege of Daeya (61–78) and Forty Fortresses (12–22). Open on Gumil's own line ('Putting a boy this green in charge of the border…' works as a provocation). Cut block 94: Euija sending Yunchung is already told in Yunchung. Move block 95 ('Pumsuk is the head general') down to sit before 127, because 116 says the True Bone hasn't arrived yet. The two passages of Maehwa walking past staring men (108–114 and 116–120) are the same beat twice, so keep one. The couple's last good night (121–126) is the emotional spine and should sit just before the arrival. The Pumsuk-on-the-pallet ending is a good hand-off to Maehwa.

## Maehwa (partly)

Pumsuk, twenty-four and married, tries to sleep instead of going back to Maehwa; he fails, and she means to teach him a lesson and ruin him a little, but ends up undone and in love; he walks out without a word, and her husband comes home.

**Fixes:** The opener ('A man is measured by his self-control') and the turn (the teacher's voice dying, the slip of his wife's name at 48–49) give it a real shape, and it stays in one place. The middle (57–74) repeats the same escalation cycle five or six times, so the stakes (Gumil at the stores, Gotaso, the fortress) drop out for the back half. Cut that run by half and keep one beat where she remembers her husband is only at the stores. The record quote (81) retells what we just watched, so cut it or move it to Siege of Daeya. The ending (he leaves without a word, then 'Morning comes. So does her husband') is a strong hand-off.

## Siege of Daeya (partly)

Gumil makes his wife tell him everything, and three weeks later he opens the granary gate to Baekje; Daeya falls, Gotaso goes with the fetch, Pumsuk surrenders on an oath and dies anyway, and Chunchu, who made him swear to protect her, asks for the road north.

**Fixes:** The core is strong: the 'everyone in this fortress is trash' callback, Gotaso and Kangrim, and Chunchu on his mother's knee. The order around the fall is scrambled. Block 40 (the news reaches the queen) comes before 41–42 (Pumsuk and Yunchung negotiating at Daeya), then 43 is back in Surabol. Move 40 after 42 and show the broken oath (bridge proposed). Mochuk (19) and Jukjuk (quote 46) appear with no setup: give Jukjuk one line in the siege or cut the quote. The episode runs on past its natural end. After Chunchu asks for the road north (56), the Bupmin gate scene (57–60) is fine, but STEAM, AGAIN (61–78) is another cavern visit. Move it to the cavern episode so this one ends on Silla's grief and the road to Pyongyang.

## Yeon’s Massacre (yes)

Yeon Gesomun has bowed all summer for his father's seal and has been given one winter on the border; at a banquet with the king he closes every door, takes the five commanders' swords onto his own back, crowns a puppet and makes himself Supreme Commander, then promises his wife none of what the world says matters.

**Fixes:** It works as its own story, with a clear want, a clear humiliation, a turn and a quiet ending. Fixes: the Bojang 'what is your name?' beat (51–53) comes after Bojang is already crowned (41–43). Move it before 41 so we watch Yeon pick the puppet. The massacre is told in a speech, then four record quotes (35, 36, 50, 54). Keep one, maybe two. The Taoist turn (55–59) is told again in Four Dragons ('The Third Leg'), so keep it in one place. The first line is a date and a death. A sharper hook would be something like 'All summer, Yeon bows.'

## Chunchu & Yeon (partly)

Chunchu, grieving his daughter, goes north to beg troops from the man who just murdered his king; Yeon names a price Chunchu won't pay, Chunchu bleeds and is jailed, a drunk favourite's turtle-and-rabbit story gives him the way out, and Yushin's march gets him released.

**Fixes:** The setup (sixty days, Hadong, 'It's you I don't trust') and the turtle story are excellent. The withheld hand wound pays off in the next episode. The ending is scrambled. 53 (Yushin counts men), 54 (narration says Yeon releases him), 55–58 (Chunchu and Yushin swapping lines before they have met), 59–62 (the reunion), then 64–68 (Yeon deciding to release him, played out a second time). Reorder it as 53 → 64–68 → 55–56, 58 (Chunchu let out) → 59–62, put Yushin's quip (57) inside the camp, and cut 54. Say the price aloud (bridge proposed). The opening news beat ('murdered by his own subject?') is repeated word for word by Euija in the next episode, so change one of them.

## Euija & Yeon (partly)

Euija goes to Pyongyang himself to buy the man who killed his king; they fight over whether kings and sun-gods are real, Euija wins Yeon with a harbour plan to cut Silla off, and Yeon admits that Euija and Chunchu frighten him the same way.

**Fixes:** The debate (politics as alchemy, the sun god) and the Chunchu-hand flashback are the episode. The journey is missing, though: block 3 is in Sabi and block 4 is at Yeon's door, so add a bridge. Euija's first line copies Sunduk's from the previous episode. 'You came with three. You're leaving with five' (49) is said before the two maids appear (51), so set up the three attendants on arrival or move 49–50 after 59. The maid tail (51–59) dilutes the ending. End instead on 'I do not yet know which of you frightens me more' / 'Flattery' / 'It was not flattery,' then the ride south (60).

## Nangbi (yes)

Yushin, thirty-four, a banner captain on a nameless horse, asks his father to let him be the collar; three charges later he sets a general's head at his father's feet, names the horse Hangyul, and in Pyongyang a Yeon father warns his son about the name.

**Fixes:** It works as a standalone, and the jump into it is set up by Euija & Yeon's last line. The only confusion is the cut from the Silla command post to the Pyongyang court (14–15), so add the header. Yeon Taejo's 'At the Colossal River' is a plant the Colossal River episode never pays off. Put young Taejo with the rolled Sui banner in that episode.

## Forty Fortresses (no)

Yushin takes more than forty Baekje fortresses, Euija panics at his name, and the cavern sisters give him three answers.

**Fixes:** This is a montage with no scene and no turn. The entry's place is set to steam_cavern. Euija's panic (1–3) has no room or listener. The Yushin–Chunchu exchange (8–10) floats. The cavern visit is the fourth in four episodes, and the closing Euija line (23) has no context. Its time is also out of order: 'over the next few years' with a 644 map, then The Eastern Star goes back to 642. Rebuild it around one scene. The best candidate is the record at quote 11, where Yushin rides past his own gate and asks only for a cup of water from home. Grow his reputation through Baekje soldiers who stop eating at his name. Move the cavern beat out and set the entry's place to the border.

## The Eastern Star (partly)

On one bright night three men (Chunchu in Surabol, Euija in Sabi, Gesomun at the sacred cave) each say out loud that they want to be the King for All.

**Fixes:** The triptych and its refrain are good. But it opens on a bare dialogue line with no place, then cuts twice with no header. Add a one-line narrator opener (e.g. 'One star, three roofs, three men who can't sleep.'). Gyebek's 'I saw Gesomun again' and the burn scar (13–14) are a plant: make sure it fires in a later Gyebek episode, or cut it.

## Emperor (no)

Far to the west, the emperor who owns half the world hears that a man called Gai Suwen has murdered his king.

**Fixes:** It is a seven-block stub, and Four Dragons replays the same beat (the report, then 'Wait. Gai Suwen…?' at block 19). Merge it into Four Dragons as the cold open and cut Four Dragons 17–21. Or keep Emperor and remove the report from Four Dragons. Don't tell it twice.

## Four Dragons (partly)

The Second Emperor, whose name no one may say, loses the one minister allowed to say no, hears Yeon's name and decides to lead the seventh invasion himself; meanwhile Silla's envoy is offered a borrowed king and a Longmen farmer is sent off to war by his wife.

**Fixes:** Taizong's want (to undo four hundred barbarian years and not repeat the Sui) is clear. Wei Zheng's death is a good obstacle that removes itself. The rest is three side stories. 'The Third Leg' repeats Yeon's Massacre 55–59, so cut it here. 'Three Choices' is a useful plant for Bidam. Longmen (47–68) is Xue Rengui's origin and would open Stallion Mountain better, where block 0 already repeats block 68. Block 20 tells the Yeon Tabal/Jolbon story before Jolbon opens it, so cut it. The 'herald' speakers (5–6) need an owner (bridge proposed).

## Yodong (partly)

The Blue Dragon walks around Goguryeo's wall of forts; Yodong, which never opened for the Sui, dresses a girl as a bride for the Holy King and still falls in twelve days.

**Fixes:** The fall of Yodong is a complete arc: the ford trick, the marsh road, the bride, the south wind. Then 15–19 jump to Ansi for the emperor and the Guardian's face-off, which spends the Ansi episode's central exchange early. 'The Rest of the Line' (20–23) then goes back in time to the fourth and fifth months. Move 14–19 into Ansi and end Yodong on the burning tower and the rest of the line. The bride (9) needs one line of setup earlier in the siege so her four words land.

## Boiling River (yes)

King Dongchun wins twice against an imperial general, rides out to win a third time on ground he never looked at, and loses his capital in an afternoon.

**Fixes:** It works as a short parable, and Yodong's last line sets up the jump in. The lesson ('I did not look at the ground') should fire in Stallion Mountain: give the Goguryeo relief commander one beat of not looking at the ground. Quote 9 calls the king 'Gung' with no gloss, which may read as a different man.

## Stallion Mountain (partly)

A farmer in white armour breaks the Goguryeo relief army and wins the emperor's favour; a Silla exile in the Tang ranks dies farther in than anyone; the farmer is captured and escapes; and Yeon's two small sons are offered titles, and the elder takes the flogging for both.

**Fixes:** There are three stories with three protagonists. Xue Rengui's arc (field to fame) is the spine, and the Longmen setup from Four Dragons should open this episode. Block 0 already duplicates Four Dragons 68. Sul Gedu is called 'Captain Xue' right before Xue Rengui appears, so rename that line or add the bridge. The capture-and-escape (26–38) restages Xue's heroism a second time and could be cut. Namseng and Namgun (39–49) are a strong plant for Brothers' Coup, but they have nothing to do with this battle's story. Move them to a flashback there or to the Ansi retreat.

## Colossal River (partly)

Ulchi Munduk surrenders seven times and runs seven times, drawing the Sui army to within thirty li of Pyongyang, then breaks it halfway across the Salsu.

**Fixes:** The jump in is set up well ('a general who surrendered seven times'), but nothing happens on stage. It is all edicts, maps, a formation and record quotes, and Munduk never speaks. Block 0 is a textbook date ('in the year 612'). Give it one scene: Munduk walking into the Sui camp (5), with the poem (8) as the letter he hands Yu Zhongwen. Put Yeon Taejo, Gesomun's father, in the Goguryeo line, riding home with a Sui banner under his arm. That pays off Nangbi 23–25, where Gesomun remembers it from when he was seven.

## Ansi (yes)

The nameless Guardian, who once kept the old king's colours on his wall in Yeon's face, holds one small fortress against the emperor; the earthen mountain falls into his wall, his men take it, winter starves the horses, and the emperor sends silk to a man whose name he never learns.

**Fixes:** It stands on its own. Bring the emperor–Guardian face-off back from Yodong 15–19, because it is this episode's argument. The arrow-and-helmet beat (24) doesn't say whose head it is (bridge proposed). 'The ring at his hip' (7) is also ambiguous. The aside about a Silla marshal (8) and 'added to the Great Heroes' (30) are textbook lines and could go. Move his last line ('you will never be crazier than we are', 35) to just before the silk (32) so the episode ends on the bow from the wall.

## Haemosu (partly)

Yuhwa, the youngest river-daughter, stays in the water when the sun god stops his chariot; she takes him into a copper room on the bank, her father throws her out, a fox leads her to Buyeo's king, and she lays an egg nobody can break.

**Fixes:** Ansi's last line sets up the jump into it. But it is Yuhwa's story under Haemosu's name, and Haemosu's exit is never shown. The quote at 70 says he left and never came back, yet his voice guides her at 64. Add one beat of him going back to the chariot and the hour resuming, so his later rescues in Buyeo and Jolbon read as a debt. Mark the arrival in Buyeo (header proposed).

## Buyeo (yes)

Jumong hatches from the egg and outshoots the princes who feed him; his mother's needle wins him the fastest horse, Daeso's knife misses, and with the river ahead and death written down for the day, his father catches the reaper's wrist and the turtles make a road.

**Fixes:** It is a complete tale, and the cavern prayer and Sosuno hook make a good card. Mark the time skips (grown men, the side room, the stable, the knife). Galsa founding his own country (25) spends a future the story never uses, so cut it or keep it to one clause. Haemosu's 'my little brother … at his new job' (67) means nothing to a first-time reader. Lady Ye's 'leave the door half open' is a good plant and needs its payoff in a later Yuri beat.

## Jolbon (partly)

Jumong, a wet exile on his knees in Tabal's hall, is made a slave to the chief's widowed daughter Sosuno; she fights wanting him all the way to a confession at the well, he splits Tabal's arrow, unites five feuding roofs, and is voted first king, with his father finally showing his face at dawn.

**Fixes:** The Sosuno romance (scenes through the hundred-paces test) is a strong standalone arc. The last forty blocks scatter it: the Pine Kingdom, a flash-forward to Jumong's death (236), Haemosu at dawn, the two sons, Sosuno's 'founding a country twice' line (252, which opens the Onjo box early), a flashback to Yuhwa's death 'five winters before' placed after scenes years later, a life-summary of Jumong's death, and an aside about the Yeon hall. End on Haemosu's dawn ('Build a world of your own') or on the Two Sons plant. Move Yuhwa's death before the dawn so the sun god comes to his son straight from her. Cut 236 and 252. Sosuno gets two cards (26 and 42), so keep one. The next-episode card ('the queen is failing… lock the door') doesn't match Gi, which opens on Chunchu sailing east. Rewrite it to tease the voyage, and mark the leap from myth back to 645.

## Gi (起) (partly)

Bidam, newly first chair, is the one hand that vetoes Princess Seungman; while Chunchu is abroad the queen collapses, the palace gate shuts on the Council, and Bidam decides—without a vote for the first time—to raise men with Yumjong.

**Fixes:** Jolbon's closing card promises "the council must name who's next", but Gi opens on Chunchu sailing east and spends 18 blocks in Yamato before the Council. Open on the Council veto ("Only one hand stays down" is the hook) and move the Yamato beat to where Bidam hears it from the harbour clerk (block 58), as a short cutaway. Haesang's send-off line ("If you reach the eastern islands…") sits after the Yamato audience; it must come before departure or be cut. The opening line "Chunchu decides to travel to the East, guided by his friend…" is a textbook caption, not a hook. Bidam reusing Chunchu's exact Yamato line to Seungman is a good callback but only lands if the reader saw Yamato first, so keep the Yamato beat short and early in the cutaway. Last beat (Gaya / six eggs) is a good jump-cue.

## Suro (partly)

A sky god falls for a mountain; their eggs become Gaya's kings; Suro, who can't speak when he sees her, marries the foreign princess Heo and lets her sons carry her name.

**Fixes:** Gi set up the question "Gaya — where did it come from?" but the episode never ties back to the word that cuts Yushin. Add one last line before the card that threads the line forward (Heo's blood → Geumgwan → a cart going to Surabol) without naming Muryuk. Two love stories stacked (Ibiga/Jeonggyeon, Suro/Heo) with the same beat (speechless man, commanding woman); trim the first. Chronology inside Heo's arrival tangles: beach → court meeting → hill rite → tent; the trouser offering to the mountain happens on landing, so move it before the court. Block 64 Heo: "It does now." answers a line that is no longer there (dangling). Suro is never the one who wants anything; give him one want (a queen nobody local can sell him).

## Seung (承) (partly)

Days 1–5 of the siege: Bidam and Yushin meet nightly for tea between the camps and argue country versus blood; Chunchu tries the conscience water on Bidam and it finds nothing, and Bidam laughs at the Sacred Bone for thinking it would.

**Fixes:** Strong spine (five pavilion nights, the splash payoff, "Blood is inevitable"). Problems: Chunchu reappears in Surabol with no word that he came back from Yamato (bridge added). The opening block is a quote record; the hook should be Seungman doing the dying queen's hair (block 4), which is already the best beat in the day. Three flashbacks (615, 636, 618) plus the Bupmin cavern detour dilute the tea; consider moving Jade Gate Valley out. Chunchu says "the Secretariat" in 647, four years before it exists (Royal Secretariat is 651). Block 64 has Korean 정자 inside the English.

## Muryuk (partly)

The youngest prince of a surrendering Gaya trades his crown for one condition: that his descendants live in Silla without shame.

**Fixes:** Too thin to stand alone (20 blocks) and opens in the wrong war: 562 Sadaham taking Daegaya, then jumps back thirty years to Geumgwan without a marker. Open on the cart rolling into Surabol (532) and move the Sadaham beat to Sadaham's own episode. The mystery-box payoff is missing: block 9 promises "before the hall, the field. The tall Gaya cone still fights" but no field is shown. That field is the cone helm watching the Baekje king die in The Severing, the reveal this episode exists for. Show it. Muryuk calling out "Yushin…" decades before Yushin is born needs the bridge (or move it to an old-man beat).

## Jeon (轉) (partly)

Days 6–9: Yushin breaks courtesy, is called a Gaya wretch, hears his Gaya dead tell him he is enough, edits heaven with a kite, kills his own horse to answer the falling star, and Bidam answers with his "because it is ours" speech.

**Fixes:** Clear emotional arc for Yushin. Days 8 and 9 hop palace → stables → scorched ground → rebel lines → rampart with no sub-headers (added). Blocks 1–2 and Muryuk's closing line all say "Sixth night" and the two cups: cut one. Day 7 opens with Bidam in the cavern without saying how a besieging commander slipped away; one clause would fix it. Ending: Bidam's speech is the climax but the episode is Yushin's; consider closing on Hanseul being named and putting the speech last in Day 9 as-is (it already is) with the card teasing Seohyun. Fine.

## Seohyun (yes)

A Gaya prince's polite son keeps getting his horse lost outside a Sacred Bone gate; the princess lifts her own bar, escapes her father's locked house through a drain in a storm, and they raise a boy with seven stars on his back.

**Fixes:** Best-structured in this range: clear want (her), obstacle (Sukhuljong, the word Gaya), turn (lightning and the drain), payoff (the name shouted at the gate, the crooked headband). Minor: the last scene label says Daeyang/대량주 while the text says Daeya; pick one. The cavern sequence is long for an origin coda; trim the fox/grandmother tryouts. Cut the Manmyung–Munhee sister aside in block 154 or keep it to one clause.

## Gyeol (結) (partly)

Day 10: Yushin kills Bidam on the old score (109), orders his house erased with Bidam's own words, sits with the dying queen who asks him to say "Dukman", and goes back alone to the empty pavilion.

**Fixes:** Bidam dies twice. Blocks 9–14 kill him and Kangrim reads his name; blocks 15–24 are the horse and the purge order; then 25–28 Kangrim walks him again and "Bidam falls the way a Hwarang falls". Move 25–27 straight after 14 and cut 28's fall (keep only the kite burning out, which also needs a plant: the "opposite kite" was never set up). Field → deathbed has no cue (header added). Block 55 says "remembers the first day of the rebellion" but the flashback is 612, the first day at the Hwarang hall; fix the wording. Sunduk's deathbed is beautiful and is the true ending; the pavilion and the "You Gaya wretch" echo work as the coda.

## Queen Jinduk (no)

The last Sacred Bone is crowned in a padded crown and cannot stop being compared to her cousin.

**Fixes:** No turn and no scene: two near-identical investiture quotes (cut one), a card with a king number in the sub ("신라 제28대 임금"), and floating lines to Yushin and Chunchu with no room (bridge added). Give her one decision: she is the one who chooses to send Chunchu west, which is what the closing card promises anyway. Build the scene at the loom at night with Chunchu: she asks him to go, he says he already packed. Then the closing card earns "Chunchu goes west…!". The goldsmith padding the crown is the right first beat; keep it.

## Huangdi (皇帝) (partly)

Chunchu goes to Chang'an to borrow an army; he asks the emperor's true name, learns the machine that makes one brush rule a continent, finds that Saluzi is a horse, wins a promise of Baekje and a poem duel, is frightened by Wu, and gets home only because On Gunhae wears his hat.

**Fixes:** The spine is excellent: "What is the correct name for me to call Your Majesty?" pays off in The Last Game with "Li Shimin". But 260 blocks bounce between too many detours: ward register, Ministry rolls, history office plus Qin book-burning flashback, Academy, clan register, Gija & Wiman flashback, two Wu scenes. Cut or move: Gija & Wiman belongs in the Dangun / Old Joseon run, not here. Reorder the end: banquet (night) → hallway with Wu ("a banquet is still going") → last game → parcel morning → Mingde Gate; right now the parcel morning sits between the banquet and the night hallway. Block 3 ("In Chang'an he watches a machine…") comes before he arrives; drop it or move after the audience. Block 6 mentions "the second banner" with no first banner. Block 162 "The Second Emperor reveals he is dying." is a placeholder caption; show it (a cough into the sleeve, a physician at the gallery door). The HALLWAY label is all caps; make it "The Hallway".

## Royal Secretariat (partly)

Chunchu routes power around the Harmony Council by building a one-seal office that answers only to the throne, then dresses the court in Tang robes but keeps the crowns.

**Fixes:** No opponent on stage: the Council never speaks, so the reform has nothing to beat. Put one uncle in the room (or let the three-month petition be the spine: open on it circling, close on it landing at the Secretariat in one afternoon). Block 12 "Today, the king will reinvent the kingdom" and block 14 "Chunchu establishes…" read as if he is already king; in 651 he is not. Blocks 4 and 13 repeat "a table that has never held a feast". Bupmin's itchy collar (43) should come before he sails (40). The Tang edict at block 50 reads as Yamato's without a header (added). The year shows as undefined in the dump; set the entry year.

## Jiabeng (駕崩) (partly)

The Second Emperor dies; twenty-one-year-old Li Zhi takes the seal and stops the war his father ordered him to stop; Chunchu decides the war is now his; Wu watches a seal change hands, is shaved, and looks up at the new emperor from the nuns' second row.

**Fixes:** Whose story? Li Zhi's grief and Wu's rise compete, and Sabi and Surabol cameo in between. Order is the real problem: Chang'an (5th month) → Sabi → Surabol (8th month) → back to the Chang'an anteroom on the death day, unmarked (header added). Better: keep the whole Chang'an thread together (deathbed → anteroom → Ganye temple) and end on Chunchu reading the Liaodong line ("Then it is mine") as the last scene before the card. Cut the two Sabi blocks or move them to Exile. Two quotes repeat the same will; keep one.

## King Muyeol (partly)

Jinduk dies; the council that Chunchu hollowed out crowns him by the same unanimity; Munhee becomes queen; Yushin fears a grudge; Chunchu writes to Zhi and does not mention Wu.

**Fixes:** The great beat is told, not shown: block 9 summarizes a holdout and the quote at 10 is Alchun declining the throne himself, which the page never explains. Dramatize it: the council offers it to Alchun first, he refuses, and laughs the room into Chunchu. Yushin's "private grudge" line has nothing to react to (bridge added). Sub on the card carries a king number ("신라 제29대 임금"). Block 7 "Queen Jinduk is dead" repeats what Kangrim just showed; cut it. The monologue about Wu's eyes is a strong closing beat; consider ending there rather than on the court summary at 26.

## Jahee (partly)

Bupmin, sent to keep a harbour ledger, is corrected by the customs officer's daughter and kisses her under a rain-curtain while her father coughs and pretends not to see.

**Fixes:** Sweet but no obstacle: he wants her, she wants him, the father allows it in one cough. Let the bad sum cost something (a ship mis-tided, a cargo lost) so her correction matters. The second scene (The Next King) skips two reigns in one sentence and calls back "king for all", a line the reader has not heard yet in reading order; either plant it in this episode first or cut the exchange. Opening is fine.

## Hyukgose (partly)

Six chiefs see a white horse kneel at a well; from its egg comes a boy they crown; he marries the dragon-born Alyoung for love, and Silla is founded on a promise that no one will be left outside the gate.

**Fixes:** The horse-and-egg discovery is told four times (blocks 0, 2–3, 5 quote, 6–13, 11 quote). Cut the opening summary and the first quote; start at the ridge with Alpyung asking why a horse is kneeling. Block 0 says "After the fall of Old Joseon", which opens the Old Joseon box before Dangun's episode; drop it. The founding manifesto (18–22) is spoken by nobody (bridge added; better, turn it into chiefs' dialogue). The best beat (the body falling in five pieces, "Nobody records a horse") is a good ending; keep.

## Talhae (yes)

A boy who washes up in a chest picks the best house in town, fakes his way into owning it with buried charcoal, and later makes the man he robbed his chief minister.

**Fixes:** Clear con-man tale with a good runner ("Prove it."). The Gaya version with Suro is a fun callback but needs a header to separate it from the Silla beach (added). Block 1 (Dapana backstory) plus its quote tell the same thing; keep one. Last beat links neatly to Alji.

## Alji (partly)

King Talhae, once a boy in a box, finds another boy in a gold box under a crowing rooster and raises him, and the Kim name begins.

**Fixes:** Fine as a short myth coda; Talhae's "Mine was bigger" is the hook. Each event is told twice (narration + quote at 3/4, 5/7, 8/9); cut the paired quotes per the one-quote rule. No one wants anything; give Alji one gesture (he doesn't ask for the throne, on screen). The steam-word plant (block 11) is good. Closing card jumps back to Baekje; fine.

## Exile (partly)

With the queen dead and the king bound by three years of mourning, Baekje's two feuding great houses make a one-night truce to remove the king's clanless champion Gyebek; bribes fail, an arrow misses, so they exile him under the king's own borrowed seal, and he washes up on Tamla, where an island king starts telling him stories.

**Fixes:** The plot is strong but told out of order and twice: block 9 already puts him on the ship before the monastery meeting, and 'put on a boat' plus the 'Satek water at the berth / Yunbi winter contract' line recur at 41 and 52. Cut block 9, and make 41 the hand-off into the reading scene (45–52). Blocks 42 ('Nine, by then') and 43 (the aphorism) are orphans; cut them or tie 42 to a counted attempt. The Euija rage (70–74) sits between island scenes; either give it its own Sabi header (proposed) or move it to Coup's opening, where it would also explain why he purges. Timeline conflict: this episode has Euija finish three years of mourning, yet Coup and Descent are dated 655–656, and Gyebek spends five years on Tamla. Pick one count. Block 93's speaker is undefined (a fisher). The last beat ('First night on the island… two suns') rewinds four years after 'Four years from now'; turn it into a bold next-episode card that says we are going back to that first night.

## Heaven–Earth King (yes)

On Gyebek's first night on Tamla, Yuri Dora tells how a god's twin sons shot down the extra sun and moon, then how the younger cheated his honest brother out of the living world, so the elder took the dead.

**Fixes:** Clean, funny, self-contained, and the jump in is set up by Exile's last line. Its weakness is that the frame vanishes for 90 blocks: add the 'Two Suns' and 'The Fire' headers so the reader knows when we leave and return to the island. The closing 'Rice with sand in it' is a perfect payoff; keep it.

## Sulmun (partly)

Mending a roof, Gyebek hears how the giantess built the island and lost her sons, and how her bridge to the mainland failed for one roll of silk; the literal man fixes on being 'one short'.

**Fixes:** Gyebek cites 368 hills nobody mentioned (bridge proposed). The silk-bridge beat is told twice (narration 14 plus quote 15); keep one. The 'one roll short' line wants a later payoff, perhaps one man short at the Yellow Mountain.

## Three Princes (partly)

The island's founding (three princes from the earth, three brides from a box) and the hunter-god divorce, and in between Gyebek meets ordinary Tamla kindness that will keep him five years.

**Fixes:** Two myths and one present-day beat with no through-line. Mark the haenyeo beat with a header (proposed). Give Gyebek one want, such as the question 'the part where he comes home'; that is the strongest moment, so end the episode near it rather than on the card. Yuri Dora interjects inside the myth at block 6 without a frame cue; harmless, but a narration line before it would help.

## Stone Lady (partly)

Three unkind tales (the magistrate who looked back, the cliff goddess who returned to stone, the daughter thrown out who was the family's luck) and Gyebek reading each as a rule.

**Fixes:** An anthology, not a story. The title belongs to Sanbangdeok, whose tale is the thinnest (four blocks), and her husband is tagged 'herald' (block 12); fix the speaker. Block 2 teases Kangrim, but it is buried as a parenthesis; either cut it or make it the closing hook. Consider retitling for Gameunjang, the tale Gyebek reacts to most.

## Gardener (yes)

A servant boy, Hallakgungi, finds his father's flower field and restores his murdered mother, then Jacheongbi beats a rule with its wording and fetches back her dead lover; Gyebek asks whether the dead can be fetched back.

**Fixes:** Works as a pair with a clear frame (orchard, then rain-doorway). Data fix: the card at block 5 uses person 'sara' but is captioned Hallakgungi, and 'sara' speaks as Hallakgungi at 35. Gyebek's last question is a good plant for the Yellow Mountain; keep it.

## Kangrim (yes)

A living magistrate's runner fetches the judge of the dead, is split between both worlds, and loses the death-ledger to a crow, which is why no one knows his hour.

**Fixes:** Self-contained and the key origin for every death scene. Blocks 2, 5, 15 and 17 are very long summary paragraphs; break each into two or three beats with one line of dialogue. Add the 'Road Down' header.

## Tribute (partly)

In 498 Tamla forgets its oranges, Baekje marches to the shore and stops, and the island owes a favour, which is why it takes Baekje's exiles.

**Fixes:** A six-block footnote with no character. Fold it into Exile at the moment the boat leaves ('there is an island, and the island owes it a favour') or into Gyebek's first night, and cut the episode. Its card 'Meanwhile in Sabi' jumps forward 157 years; if kept, mark the jump back.

## Coup (partly)

Euija, finally free of the clans' grip, stages martial law and an enabling law, replaces the whole Assembly with forty-one sons, and turns a Satek into his Premier; then that Premier tells the Tang emperor Baekje will fall on its own.

**Fixes:** The turn is great but the episode never shows why Euija acts now; open on his rage over Gyebek's exile (move Exile 70–74 here) so the purge is revenge with a face. The martial-law speeches (3–8, 13–14) are modern-statute pastiche at length; cut to two lines and let Chunbok's wet-ink joke carry it. Block 28 needs setup (bridge proposed). The Chang'an coda (37–42) has no header, time or reason Chunbok is there; mark it, or move it to Descent as a cold-open betrayal. Block 21–22 (Ye Sikjin's drawer) is a good plant; keep it.

## Descent (partly)

The king who beat eight houses can't sleep: he drinks, exiles Heungsu, drowns in a harem, and starves the one minister (Seongchung) who demands open court, then ignores his dying letter.

**Fixes:** Blocks 14–24 are image-prompt shot lists ('They hike the silk. One knee up. A twist.'), which the narration rules forbid; cut them to one paragraph and the maids' dialogue. Mark Gomamiji and the cell (headers proposed). The speaker 'nation-baekje' at 39 has no identity. The best story spine is Seongchung (entrance at 45, death at 51–56); plant him earlier (one line in Coup or at 7–8) so his death lands.

## Nine Omens (yes)

Chunchu manufactures nine omens to break Baekje's nerve; Euija, a lifelong maker of fake miracles, kills the shaman who reads them truly, can't admit they were made, and finally jumps into the White River and wakes up: 'Summon Gyebek'.

**Fixes:** Strong arc with a real turn. The omens are told twice (numbered list 2–10 plus the omens block 11); keep the list or the block, not both. Move the Surabol flashback (12) to just after block 1 so the reader knows the omens are made before seeing them, or keep it after for irony but add the headers. The Yamato quote (25) is a stray; cut it.

## Onjo (partly)

When Jumong's first son walks in with half a sword, Sosuno takes her two boys south rather than live in a footnote; a white stag leads them to Mount Buak, Biryu chooses the sea, and Onjo founds Baekje.

**Fixes:** A complete founding tale, but the jump in from 'Summon Gyebek!' is jarring and the jump out ('two armies… a dead man's letter') points at the wrong episode. Opening says 'Nobody there ever mentions Buyeo' and then cuts to Buyeo; headers proposed. Block 38 summarises the stag arrival before block 39 tells it; cut 38. The explicit grain-room scene (26–34) runs long against the rest; trim it so the farewell at 35–36 stays the emotional peak.

## Sungchung (no)

With two armies converging, Euija bullies Chunbok into sending Gyebek out with too few men, while Ye Sikjin quietly does his own sums.

**Fixes:** Eight blocks, titled for a man who died two episodes ago and never appears. The previous card promises 'a dead man's letter', so open on Seongchung's letter being read aloud in the panicking court and keep the title, or merge this into Heungsu as its cold open. 'Send General Gyebek' is premature: he is still on Tamla until the next two episodes; reorder so the summons comes first.

## Heungsu (partly)

The exiled minister who drew the same map every morning for four years is asked for a plan, says 'Seongchung already wrote it', is ignored, and walks north toward a pass already crossed.

**Fixes:** The Gomamiji flashback and the courier scene are the best writing in the range. The first flashback is labelled 655 'The berth', but Gyebek talks about marching to the Yellow Mountain, which is 660 and after his exile; either redate it to 660 or rewrite it as the 655 farewell. The return to the present (block 3) needs a header (proposed). The card ('a boat is coming for the Turtle') repeats Gyebek's block 2 nearly word for word.

## Gyebek (partly)

In his fifth year on Tamla the boat comes; Gyebek refuses comfort, promises Yuri Dora he will not forget people, goes home, kills his own family so the Tang can't enslave them, and rides for the Yellow Mountain.

**Fixes:** The emotional middle is missing: he was summoned by the king who named him, but the episode never shows Euija and Gyebek together. Add one short reunion beat at Sabi between the shore and home; it is the payoff of the whole Exile arc. Block 0 starts on the island with no place cue. The family-killing (15–16) arrives with no setup; one line of Gyebek seeing the odds first would earn it.

## Three Realms (partly)

At heaven's annual pavilion meeting, gods gossip and flirt while Kangrim quietly asks the Gardener if the dead can be brought back, and the brothers note mortals talk of reuniting Dangun's land.

**Fixes:** It opens 'Epilogue · Part II', which is wrong here, placed between Gyebek's march and the battle. Retitle the opener. The Samsin/Haemosu sex chatter (12–17) is a long detour; cut it to one exchange so Kangrim's resurrection question, the real plant, is the centre. The 'crucify' joke is out of world. Placement breaks the march → battle momentum; consider moving it after Yellow Mountain, so Kangrim's question follows Gyebek's death.

## Yellow Mountain (yes)

Five thousand men who have already waved at death hold three camps against fifty thousand, win four times, until two Silla boys die on purpose and their fathers' grief breaks the line; Kangrim asks Gyebek his question and Gyebek finishes his duty.

**Fixes:** The best-structured episode in the range: clear clash headers and a count. Fixes are local. 'And theirs? / Fifty thousand, my lord' (34–35) are both tagged Gyebek. Yushin speaks at 45 with no arrival (bridge proposed), and later rides out alone again at 66; keep the second. Block 122 repeats 112's 'unfinished weather' line. Block 127 ('gaozong: ?') is an orphan; cut it. The Thermopylae aside (42) breaks period voice.

## Sabi (partly)

Euija tries to feed off the Tang, flees to Bear Fortress, and is sold to the Red Fowl by the Ye brother he never seated, while his son kneels, the palace women jump, and Chunchu makes him pour the wine.

**Fixes:** Ye Sikjin's arc (the drawer from Coup, 'Which seat?', the charcoal count) is a great self-contained betrayal and should be the spine. Cut the 'KIM CHUNCHU!!!' shout (16–19); it appears again in Buyeo Euija† with its setup, and here Chunchu answers 'Hm?' from nowhere. Move the maid lines and the second Falling Flower line (55–58) up next to the cliff scene (25–27). Seven quotes in a row (48–54) stall the climax; keep one or two. Headers proposed for the flight, the gate, the feast and the two camps.

## Buyeo Euija† (partly)

In Chang'an the captive king reads aloud a confession he mocks as a bad story, signs it, curses Chunchu across the sea, and dies asking for an avenger, with Kangrim reminding him of the boy he named.

**Fixes:** The confession scene (3–8) is excellent. Death arrives with two escorts (Haewonmek at 19–22, then Kangrim at 23–26) and no cue; bridge proposed, or drop Haewonmek. The narration after death runs fourteen blocks of epitaph, some repeating themselves (27–30, 32–33, 39); keep 35–38 and cut the rest. Block 35 says he spoke at forty-one to a boy he named, but he named Gyebek at thirty-two; fix it. Block 40 spends a future reveal (Kyun Hwon, 240 years); trim to the tease in 30.

## Kim Chunchu† (yes)

Dying at fifty-eight with half the job done, Chunchu admits the war was for his daughter, hands his son the dream 'a king for all', and walks west with Kangrim.

**Fixes:** Works. The opener at a temple and the deathbed are different rooms (header proposed). Block 3 restates Buyeo Euija†'s closing card almost verbatim; cut one. Parenthetical ages (Munhee (55), Bupmin (35), Muyeol (58)) and the regnal table read as textbook. Blocks 17–18 repeat each other.

## Ungjin Commandery (partly)

The Tang net Baekje into commanderies under a cheerful disgraced old general, demote Silla's king to a prefectural clerk, and Gaozong, coached by Wu Zetian, picks four generals to finish his father's war on Goguryeo.

**Fixes:** Well-headed, but no protagonist: four short scenes in three countries. Make Munmu's 'sign as its clerk, and keep a copy' the spine and end on it, or give Liu Rengui a want. Two diagrams plus a table for the Four Beasts (25–27) is one too many. Gaozong's edict (29) is archival text in a mouth; shorten it. The card hands off to Pung well.

## King Pungjang (partly)

Rebel general Boksin buys back Baekje's exiled prince from Yamato with a hundred Tang prisoners, stages a roll call on the beach that goes comically wrong, and finds the king he crowned already slipping out of his hands.

**Fixes:** The Roll Call is a delightful standalone scene. The episode buries it: it opens on a 371 sword flashback, and Boksin and the restoration are never set up (bridge proposed; better, move the flashback after the Asuka scene, where the 'favour' is asked). Block 7 says the empress 'dies the next year', but block 9 is 661, the same year; fix the order. Blocks 42–45 restate the same Boksin–Pung rift four times; keep one. The Pisong beat is told backwards (block 50 says they moved back before 51–52 argue the move); reorder to argue, move, and return. The card says 'Baekje has its king back' after an episode about him not really being king; sharpen it to the rift.

## Pyongyang I (partly)

The empire tries Pyongyang again: Wu Zetian talks Gaozong out of going himself, the Red Fowl sits down before the walls, Namseng loses the frozen Amnok and is cursed by his father, and the starving Tang army begs Silla for rice until old Yushin volunteers to drive it north.

**Fixes:** It has no protagonist; it hops Pyongyang → Luoyang → Taedong → Amnok → Pyongyang → Surabol in 19 blocks, half of them summary. Pick one spine. Best candidate: Namseng, the heir who loses one river and hears 'I gave you one river' (it plants the brothers' war). Cut the textbook line 'The impenetrable walls of Pyongyang are tested once again' and the duplicate Tang quote (blocks 10 and 11 tell the same crossing). Put block 13 (Red Fowl freezing) straight after block 8 so the siege is one beat. The Yushin offer is a strong last beat; it should end on him loading the carts, and the Rice Road payoff (now at the end of Snake River) should move here or be cut there.

## Snake River (partly)

Yeon Gesomun counts the White Tiger's thirteen sons into the Snake River one by one, kills the father, outfaces Yumla's two reapers in the middle of the fight, and the empire hands the dead man's title to Xue Rengui; then Yushin's rice reaches the starving Tang.

**Fixes:** The countdown is the best set piece in the range and works on its own. Three things break it: (1) 'Yumla Defied' happens during the fight but is placed after the father dies and after a cut to the far west; move blocks 38–48 to just before block 25 ('Then only the tiger is left') so the reapers come at the worst hour and Gesomun's 'Not today' powers the last kill; (2) the Xue Rengui coda (34–37) should come last, after the river, as the empire's answer; (3) the Rice Road (49–54) belongs to Pyongyang I, where Yushin volunteers; here it dilutes the Gesomun ending. A better last beat is Gesomun's 'I am… none other than… Yeon Gesomun!!' followed by Xue taking the name.

## Tamla Surrenders (no)

After the Snake River, the island kingdom of Tamla quietly switches from Baekje to Silla and the Tang.

**Fixes:** Six blocks: two lines of summary, two archival quotes and an end card. Nobody wants anything on the page. Either fold it into White River (block 61 already sends a Tamla envoy up the hill at Juryu, which is the dramatic moment of the switch) or give it a scene: Yuri Dora's envoy weighing three banners on a beach, a one-line bargain, the quote. Its end card repeats Rebellion's opening almost word for word ('Baekje is supposed to be finished. Nobody told the fortresses'); keep it in one place only.

## Rebellion (partly)

A True Bone general, Kim Jinju, calls in sick for the campaign against a Baekje holdout and is seen at a gyuku match; young Munmu beheads him and his household, and his son in Chang'an quietly decides to wait for a ship.

**Fixes:** Clean shape (sin, judgment, seed of revenge) and the Punghun plant pays off in Maeso. It opens on a header and a summary instead of a hook; open on Jinju's line 'Nineteen generals for one hill fort. They don't need a twentieth.' Cut the archival detour (blocks 12–13 on 'two men of the name'); it is a textbook aside that undercuts the execution. Jinheum is a second name the reader never meets again; drop him from the narration.

## Betrayal (partly)

Flashback: Boksin and the monk Dochim share the restoration until Dochim gets grand, so Boksin murders him at supper; two years later Boksin plots against King Pung, is caught, spits at his accuser and ends up pickled in a jar while Sangji and Sangya watch and think about switching sides.

**Fixes:** Good arc (the kingmaker eaten by his king) and well set up by Rebellion's 'we have to go back'. Problems: block 1 says 'Before Boksin and the king' but block 7 has Pung already crowned, so the frame is wrong; say 'In the first year of the king'. Block 14 ('Boksin plots to kill the king by pretending to be sick, but is caught and executed instead') is a plot summary that spends the twist before block 15 dramatizes it; cut it. Block 15 cites 'the sixth month of 663', which the next block already implies; drop the year. It overlaps King Pungjang's last third (Boksin resenting the king, the move to Pisong); trim one of them.

## White River (yes)

Four banners meet at one river mouth: King Pung abandons Juryu to feast a Yamato fleet, Liu Rengui anchors a wall of ships and waits for the tide, Takutsu dies on a burning deck, Pung flees north leaving his sword, and his elder brother Yung, on the Tang flagship, names it and lets him go.

**Fixes:** Strong, with dated scene headers and a real emotional spine (Yung vs Pung). The 'Four Banners' scene is a long overview (blocks 4–9) before anyone speaks; cut the Silla roster numbers ('twenty-eight generals… thirty in another copy') and move straight from Boksin's jar to Pung's announcement. Block 2 ('The epic battle: for the first time the West, Samhan, and the East meet…') is a trailer card; cut it. The tail after Juryu (Imjon and the Yushin/Liu alliance) is three summaries; end on the refugees' quote ('The name of Baekje ends today') or on Sangji's 'I built it', not on the alliance aside.

## Yeon Gesomun† (partly)

The Eternal General, who has refused death once, waits for the reapers and gets Yumla himself; he dies in his sleep telling his sons not to fight, and the narrator weighs a man who was right about everything and built nothing.

**Fixes:** The Yumla deathbed works and is set up by the Snake River. The middle is muddy: the uncle Jungto and Namgun's two lines (18–20) are unstaged, and Namgun's 'If the old man were alive we would not be in this state' is a line from after the coup that hasn't happened yet. The epitaph (block 25) re-tells the last-words exchange we just watched, and block 26 spoils the next episode ('his eldest was riding west to show the Third Emperor the road in'). Cut 25, cut the spoiler half of 26, and end on 'He had three sons. How long do you think that lasts?'

## Brothers’ Coup (partly)

Namseng, the new Supreme Commander, tours the provinces; whisperers turn his two brothers against him, a spy is caught, the gate of Pyongyang is shut in his face, and he rides west to kneel to the emperor his father fought.

**Fixes:** The arc is clear but it opens with an unstaged imperial edict in Gaozong's mouth (an archival speech; turn it into a two-line scene or a quote). Block 8 ('A messenger comes to the provincial camp…') adds nothing between the spy's capture and the shut gate; cut it. The killing of Namseng's son exists only inside a quote (block 16); that is the emotional turn of the episode and should be a narrated beat. The gate scene (10–14) ends in Namseng's Joseon speech, which is fine as a plant. The uncle Jungto coda splits the ending; end on Namseng's 'ten thousand years' and the end card.

## Pyongyang II (partly)

Three Tang 'beasts' close on Pyongyang with Namseng as guide; Namgun trusts the one man he thinks can't be bought, a monk, who opens the gate; Namgun botches his suicide, the king bows at Zhaoling, and in Silla Munmu invents a rank for Yushin.

**Fixes:** Shinsung's betrayal is the real story and is good. The opening is a jumble of one-line voices (Xue, Namsan, Namseng, Namgun) with no setting, and Namgun's 'Goguryeo… never dies….!' appears twice (blocks 8 and 21); cut the first. Block 16 re-states the gate opening in textbook form right after block 15; cut it. The Yushin promotion is a separate story; it can stay as a coda, but the end card ('The final war begins…!') leads into Mount Gain, which goes back three years. See Mount Gain: this episode should instead end on the Dangun lead-in ('to a bear in a cave…!').

## Mount Gain (yes)

The empire makes Munmu swear brotherhood with Buyeo Yung, the Baekje prince he once spat on, over a white horse, and the only white horse in camp is Yushin's old Hanseul; Yushin walks him up the hill himself.

**Fixes:** A complete, moving story: want (keep the land), obstacle (the oath), cost (the horse), last line ('Find me a war instead'). Its problem is placement: it is 665, but it is read after Pyongyang II (668), where Yushin has already been made Supreme General, so the reader jumps back three years with no warning. Move it to sit right after White River (or between White River and Yeon Gesomun†), give it a new end card teasing Gesomun's deathbed, and give Pyongyang II the bear-in-a-cave lead-in. If it must stay, its first line needs to say it is going back ('Three years before the city fell…'). Also: blocks 1 and 8 give two different time markers ('Two springs after the river', 'The next summer'); keep one.

## Dangun & Old Joseon (partly)

Myth: heaven's son Hwanung comes down to Mount Taebaek, a bear outlasts a tiger to become a woman and corners him under the birch, their son Dangun founds Joseon; two thousand years later the Han besiege Wanggeom and the city falls because someone inside lifts the bar.

**Fixes:** The jump into it is well set up by Mount Gain's last line. Internally, block 7 ('The long way begins… with a bear') is followed by block 8 ('From there he hands out civilisation') whose 'he' is Hwanung; swap 7 and 8 so the bear line leads into the bear. The two halves (a romance, a siege) are separate stories glued by one header; the siege half is the one the book needs (it plants 'a door opened from the inside' and the six villages of Surabol). Either split the Fall of Joseon into its own short episode or open the episode on the siege and tell the bear as Ugeo's bedtime memory.

## Anseung (partly)

After Pyongyang falls, Geom Mojam raises the old flag and crowns a royal cousin, Anseung; they quarrel over whether to fight, Anseung has him killed and takes the survivors south, and Munmu makes him King of Goguryeo inside Silla to annoy the emperor.

**Fixes:** The murder and Munmu's 'Give him a seal. A big one' are good beats, but two back-to-back quotes (3–4) state the setup twice before anyone speaks; keep one. The flight to Silla is missing (see bridge). Opening line repeats Dangun's end card ('Nearly eight hundred years after Wanggeom, the empire… does the same thing again'); open on the quarrel instead. The episode needs one more beat of Anseung himself: a guest-room king with a borrowed seal is a character, and right now he is only a decision.

## Letters (yes)

Xue Rengui tries to win the war by post; Munmu stays up all night dictating a reply that lists every debt Tang owes Silla, the two men trade shorter and ruder notes, and Munmu answers the last one by capturing seventy rice ships.

**Fixes:** Works well and pays off Snake River, Mount Gain and Rebellion. Two clean-ups: block 29 opens 'He comes.' but it is Silla that strikes, not Xue who arrives; change to 'He does not come. His rice does.' Daeto's second letter (block 22) is a good plant that fires in Kim Yushin†; keep it. The episode could end on 'Late. As usual.' and drop the extra card line about chasing.

## Stone Gate (no)

Silla and the Goguryeo remnants beat the Tang, chase them, and are routed at Seokmun; Silla sends a grovelling apology and starts building, following a plan Chunchu laid out years ago.

**Fixes:** No one on the page wants anything; it's a battle summary, two quotes, a formation box and a flashback. The human story of Stone Gate is Wonsul, who is in the next episode. Merge the two: open on Wonsul in the chase, Danneung grabbing his bridle at the gate, and use Chunchu's flashback as Munmu's reason for the apology. If kept separate, open with a hook instead of 'The Tang take Hansi and Mapeup and come south.'

## Wonsul (partly)

Yushin's son survives a rout he was told to die in; his father disowns him and asks the king to execute him, the king refuses, and Wonsul goes to work another man's fields under no name.

**Fixes:** A complete little tragedy, but it starts in summary ('is told to die there and does not'), and the 'there' depends on the previous episode. Open on a live beat: Danneung's hand on the bridle, or the closed gate. Block 4 is a narrator lecture on Gaya assimilation that Yushin's own line ('Another man's son may retreat. Mine may not.') already says; cut it. The farmer exchange is a good last beat.

## Kim Yushin† (partly)

Old Yushin's last visit to the steam cavern, then his deathbed: the king comes, Kangrim asks his question, Munhee asks if he is a Silla man now, Daeto is caught, and after the funeral Wonsul's mother refuses him too.

**Fixes:** The pieces are strong, but the cavern and the deathbed share one 'day' header (block 0); add a scene header at the deathbed. 'Princess…' needs a cue (bridge). The epitaph (25–30) is long and partly repeats Munhee's question; trim to two paragraphs. The Daeto execution (24) lands in the middle of the funeral; move it after the epitaph or into Wanggeom's Guest so the death stays the last big beat before Lady Jiso.

## The Wanggeom's Guest (partly)

After the funeral Munmu finds his uncle's secret spring, the three goddesses lose their composure over him, pronounce that the west will take his name, and Dangun himself appears on the water to hand him the old title of Wanggeom.

**Fixes:** The visit has a turn (comedy to oracle to Dangun) but no stake: Munmu asks one question and leaves. Give him a want he walks in with (whether to break the oath of Mount Gain, or whether to fight the Tang at sea), so the oracle answers it. Blocks 1 and 5 both say 'the best of both' and repeat 'Gaya shoulders / Surabol mouth' three times; cut the repeats. The end card ('Kim Punghun said he could wait for a ship. The ship is here') is a good bridge into Maeso.

## Maeso (yes)

Xue Rengui lands with Punghun as his pilot; a Silla general lets the horses unload and then cuts the beach to pieces, and at Maeso the Silla army steals thirty thousand Mohe horses in a night, with the disgraced Wonsul leading the cut.

**Fixes:** Clear and fun, and it pays off Rebellion and Wonsul. The 'heads?' / 'horses' exchange is a great button. Wonsul's return (block 24) is told in one long paragraph; give him one line or one action on the picket line so the payoff is seen. Punghun is named as pilot and never appears again; either give him a beat on the deck or drop him from the opener. Two closing quotes (34–35) contradict each other on purpose; keep one.

## Final Ford (partly)

At the mouth of the Geum, a middling captain loses twice to Xue Rengui's fleet, lures it onto the mudflats the third time, and the Tang ships turn west and do not come back.

**Fixes:** Short and clean, but Sideuk is a cipher and Xue never appears in his own last battle. One exchange between Xue and his helmsman as the hulls ground would close his arc (he has been the farmer since Snake River). The formation box and the quote say the same thing; keep one. Ending on Munmu's 'Have we… won…?' works.

## The King for All (yes)

Munhee straightens her son's collar on the day he becomes king of all Samhan; five years later he is burned and put under a rock in the sea, and eleven years after that the Tang complain about his father's temple name and drop it at the name of Kim Yushin.

**Fixes:** A good closing chapter for the Silla line, and the mother-and-collar frame is the right first and last image. The two later scene headers are bare years ('681', '692'); rename them to places ('The Sea Tomb / 바다 무덤', 'The Envoy / 당 사신') so they match the other labels and avoid AD years. Block 12 ('Silla lasts nine hundred and ninety-two years') spends a fact the narrator could tease instead.

## Balhae (yes)

The winter Pyongyang falls, a Mohe father and his frozen son shelter in a cave; the boy finds a gold branch of the Goguryeo crown in the pack, and the father tells how Yeon Gesomun picked him up from a burned doorway and taught him three words.

**Fixes:** Works on its own and ends the book well; the flashback is properly marked. The map says 720 and the entry is 698 while the scene is the winter of 668; set the entry year to the scene. The coda after 'Cut to black' (31–34) is two summaries and two quotes; keep 'They walk on…' and one quote, and let THE END follow. Block 25's 'By the Holy King's bow' is a nice callback.
